### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**10** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx`  _(via sys_invitation (literal, a string literal in isPresentedInvitationPending))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via os register (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/register.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via invitationId (literal, a string literal in SIGN_UP_INVITATION_ID_FIELD; a string literal in resolveNoSignInAccountReport), invite_only (literal, a string literal in invitationProofFor; a string literal in resolveNoSignInAccountReport), sys_invitation (literal, a string literal in isPresentedInvitationPending), os register (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/register.ts))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via invite_only (literal, a string literal in invitationProofFor; a string literal in resolveNoSignInAccountReport))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via sys_invitation (literal, a string literal in isPresentedInvitationPending))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via invite_only (literal, a string literal in invitationProofFor; a string literal in resolveNoSignInAccountReport), sys_invitation (literal, a string literal in isPresentedInvitationPending))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **184** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd43416f58df30912aeba31abf78863e5731baff` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e81b68b3a493e2f81bba5bffbb13e397b85c730b` — the merge of head `83438de27397d68f296625d2f8343925df480d76` into base `cd43416f58df30912aeba31abf78863e5731baff`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e81b68b3a493e2f81bba5bffbb13e397b85c730b && git checkout e81b68b3a493e2f81bba5bffbb13e397b85c730b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cd43416f58df30912aeba31abf78863e5731baff 83438de27397d68f296625d2f8343925df480d76 && git checkout -B drift-repro cd43416f58df30912aeba31abf78863e5731baff && git merge --no-ff 83438de27397d68f296625d2f8343925df480d76

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd43416f58df30912aeba31abf78863e5731baff
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cd43416f58df30912aeba31abf78863e5731baff` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT at `Head-sha: 83438de27397d68f296625d2f8343925df480d76` (2026-11-08T22:31Z).

- **Shape:** a no-card order from the security#1 seat, in three rounds. A contract-tier reviewer approved the order before dispatch. Round 2 corrected the declaration to `Metadata-protocol: added` with `@objectstack/spec` graded `minor`. Round 3 applied the review's four edits: the release smoke presents the invitation, two checklist items, one test name, and the changeset's **Who moves.** and **Operators.** lines. 90 files, +1085 / −243. Not governed (`check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 31686`: 0 of 90 paths). `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, BREAKING, ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` · `Metadata-protocol: added` · `Skills-docs: updated here`. The title carries `!`.
- **Ruling:** the maintainer, 2026-11-08, in this seat's session, ruled option E. `invite_only` stays the default, and `open` and `email_domain` are unchanged.
- **Premise measured:**
  - Under `invite_only`, a self-serve sign-up is admitted only by the invitation it presents. Every refused state gives the identical `SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED` answer, and none writes a row.
  - The first account, an operator's seed, `open` and `email_domain` are unchanged.
  - Ablation: the by-id probe swapped back turns 2 tests red; restored. The release smoke's invited probe answers 403 with the key removed and 200 with it.
- **Gates:**
  - CI on this head: everything is `success` or `skipped` except Check Changeset. That check reads the PR body, and it re-runs on the seat's body patch; the reviewer measured exit 0 against this body offline.
  - Locally: every derived command that reaches a changed file exits 0 (145 derived).
  - Dogfood battery: green at `0729e90b58`. It is accepted for this head on input identity: the later diff touches only the changeset, the release smoke script, two checklist files and one test name, none of which the battery reads. It is NOT accepted on CI's PR-level dogfood tick. The queue's dogfood run is the head-pinned measurement, and a queue bounce goes back to the dev as a patch round.
- **Merge note:** the queue regenerates `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`; it is never hand-edited.
- **Review:** the isolated contract-tier reviewer returned APPROVE-WITH-EDITS. After round 3 it returned PASS on this head, with no further edits.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - The by-id probe is scoped to `invite_only`.
  - The request mapping is an **Upgrading.** paragraph, not a `FROM → TO` label, because the ADR-0087 gate reads that label as a migration prescription.
  - Door cases are pinned at the admission seam.
  - Extra fixture and caller files were touched so that every fixture sign-up carries the id.
- **Landing:** the seat lands it through the merge queue (`pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`).

Implemented-by: os-dev (security#1 order, `session_017xRBcT1w3zpekijraHJE4f`) · Reviewed-by: isolated contract-tier reviewers (the order, then the PR, then a same-head confirmation).
